message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) share a very distant common ancestor that belongs to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
This ancestor was a placental mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago**, before the lineages that would become Carnivora (lions, cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and Perissodactyla (horses, rhinos, zebras, tapirs, etc.) split apart. In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a generic Laurasiatherian mammal from the late Cretaceous‑early Paleogene period.
